macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: U.S. equities rallied as weak July jobs data boosted rate-cut hopes
items.summary: U.S. stocks advanced on Friday, with the S&P 500, Dow, and Nasdaq all higher; CNN reported the S&P 500 back at a record high and the Dow above 54,000. The move followed weaker-than-expected U.S. labor data, including a 23,000-job loss in July and downward revisions to prior months, which pushed Treasury yields lower and increased expectations that the Fed may have more room to avoid tightening.[12][4][18]

items.title: U.S. labor market unexpectedly weakened in July
items.summary: The U.S. economy unexpectedly lost 23,000 jobs in July, and prior payrolls were revised down by a combined 103,000 jobs in May and June. MarketWatch also reported the unemployment rate fell to 4.1%, while ADP said private employers added only 44,000 jobs, reinforcing signs of a softer labor market.[4][3][18]

items.title: China inflation data showed continued disinflation
items.summary: China’s July CPI rose 0.5% year over year, below expectations, while PPI fell 3.5% year over year, indicating persistent price weakness in the industrial sector. On a monthly basis, CPI fell 0.1%, also underscoring subdued domestic demand.[2]

items.title: Central bank commentary remained in focus ahead of key policy signals
items.summary: Trading Economics’ calendar showed a scheduled speech by Fed Hammack and an RBA Governor Bullock speech, keeping central bank communication in focus for markets. The calendar also listed multiple inflation and production releases that typically influence policy expectations.[1]

items.title: Canada added 75,000 jobs in July despite U.S.-trade uncertainty
items.summary: Statistics Canada said the economy added 75,000 jobs in July and posted a modest increase in its trade surplus in June. The New York Times said the data contrasted with the U.S. jobs decline and came amid ongoing uncertainty over trade relations with Washington.[11]

items.title: Market roundup flagged several notable company and sector developments
items.summary: MarketScreener highlighted headlines including Nvidia’s planned investment of up to $3 billion in Stargate data-center developer Lancium, Alibaba’s revenue-sharing plan with big customers for its new Qwen AI model, and China tax authority scrutiny of offshore insurance income. It also noted a Hong Kong debut surge for NASN Intelligent Tech and a CEO designation at Hang Lung Group.[6]

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin holds near $65K as spot ETF demand and softer labor data support price
items.summary: Bitcoin traded around $64,957, roughly flat over 24 hours and up 3.38% over the week, with spot ETF demand and softer U.S. labor data cited as support. Futures liquidations over the last 24 hours totaled about $1.02 million, with shorts making up most of the liquidations.

items.title: Bitcoin ETFs post strongest week since April amid renewed inflows
items.summary: Reports say U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs logged their best week since April, including BlackRock’s IBIT pulling in $479 million. Separate coverage also says Bitcoin ETFs ended July with $172.4 million in net inflows, reinforcing institutional demand.

items.title: CLARITY Act advances in the U.S. Senate, with floor vote pushed into September
items.summary: Crypto policy coverage indicates Senate leadership filed cloture and plans to move the CLARITY Act vote into September rather than before the summer recess. The bill remains one of the most closely watched U.S. crypto regulatory developments.

items.title: Brazil imposes 24-hour delay on crypto transfers above $10,000
items.summary: Brazilian regulators reportedly introduced a 24-hour hold for cryptocurrency transfers exceeding $10,000, a move aimed at tightening oversight of larger digital-asset transactions. The change adds to a week of active global crypto compliance developments.

items.title: Ripple says European expansion is ready to scale after MiCA progress
items.summary: Ripple said its regulatory groundwork in Europe is now in place and that it is shifting from approvals to scaling its business. The company framed the update as a sign that MiCA-related compliance is enabling broader expansion in the EU.

items.title: Trump Media ends Crypto.com partnership, sending CRO sharply lower
items.summary: The biggest project-level market shock in the past 24 hours was Trump Media’s decision to cancel its partnership with Crypto.com, which reportedly pushed CRO down more than 12% to a multi-year low below $0.05. The move was described as having immediate market impact on the exchange’s native token.

items.title: Bybit files RICO lawsuit against North Korea over $1.5B hack
items.summary: Bybit escalated its response to a major security incident by filing a RICO lawsuit tied to a reported $1.5 billion hack linked to North Korea. The case is notable both for its scale and for signaling more aggressive legal action from crypto firms after large breaches.

items.title: BIP-110 soft fork dispute creates uncertainty around Bitcoin network direction
items.summary: Multiple outlets reported that BIP-110 has entered mandatory signaling or begun to split support among miners, with a controversial soft-fork attempt creating debate over the network’s direction. Coverage described the situation as a significant technical and governance story for Bitcoin.

items.title: Project developments: Sui adopts post-quantum signatures, Carbon launches derivatives venue, CoinMarketCap expands RWA API
items.summary: Notable product and infrastructure updates included Sui adopting post-quantum signature schemes, Carbon launching a TradFi-native on-chain derivatives venue with 950+ markets, and CoinMarketCap expanding its Pro API with real-world asset data endpoints. These announcements point to ongoing experimentation in security, derivatives, and data infrastructure.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: OpenAI slows or pauses work on the Astra model over cybersecurity concerns
items.summary: OpenAI has reportedly suspended some work on its upcoming Astra model after internal evaluations raised concerns about its cybersecurity capabilities. The report also links the move to broader scrutiny of AI agent security after recent breach-related disclosures.

items.title: OpenAI removes ChatGPT text-chat limits for free users
items.summary: OpenAI said free and Go users can now send unlimited text chats, alongside a new 'think' button for complex queries. The change appears aimed at broadening access while pushing heavier use toward its latest model stack.

items.title: Google reshuffles DeepMind leadership
items.summary: Reports say Demis Hassabis is taking on a broader role as Alphabet chairman and chief scientist in a leadership change affecting DeepMind and Alphabet’s AI strategy. The move has been tied to concerns about Gemini delays and talent departures.

items.title: Alibaba releases Qwen3.8-Max
items.summary: Alibaba’s Qwen team has launched Qwen3.8-Max, described as a 2.4T-parameter model with a 1M-token context window and aggressive pricing. The model is being positioned as a frontier contender in agentic benchmarks.

items.title: Meta launches Muse Code
items.summary: Meta has introduced Muse Code, its first AI coding agent, along with Muse Spark 1.2 as a coding-focused model. The release targets the fast-growing market for agentic software development tools.

items.title: Anthropic reportedly signs a major cloud deal and expands cost-cutting infrastructure plans
items.summary: Anthropic is said to be pursuing a $10 billion deal with AI cloud startup Volta while also building an in-house chip team. The company’s infrastructure push is framed around reducing inference costs and scaling Claude usage.

items.title: AWS makes Bedrock AgentCore runtime generally available
items.summary: AWS has made Bedrock AgentCore runtime instances generally available for production AI agents. The service adds persistent compute, 14-day sessions, and GPU support for longer-running agent workflows.

items.title: Mistral releases Shieldstral 1.0
items.summary: Mistral has launched Shieldstral 1.0, an open-weights 3B multimodal safety classifier. The company says it can match much larger models while running on a single 16GB GPU.

items.title: Nvidia opens Alpamayo 2 Super for commercial use
items.summary: Nvidia has made Alpamayo 2 Super available commercially under the OpenMDW-1.1 license. The model is described as a frontier open reasoning model for robotaxis and autonomous vehicles.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: Quake gets a free 30th-anniversary expansion
items.summary: id Software and MachineGames released a free update for Quake Remastered called "Dawn of the Machine," adding new maps and mechanics to mark the franchise’s 30th anniversary. The update is one of the biggest retro-game-related announcements in the past day.

items.title: Minecraft on Switch 2 gets an October release date
items.summary: Mojang confirmed that the native Nintendo Switch 2 version of Minecraft will launch on 27 October 2026. The announcement is one of the most notable console-release updates in the last 24 hours.

items.title: Rockstar sets a new GTA 6 presentation for 27 August
items.summary: Rockstar Games announced an extended look at Grand Theft Auto VI, with the presentation set to debut on Netflix before YouTube. The reveal is one of the biggest industry news items in the past day.

items.title: EA acquisition closes with $20 billion in debt
items.summary: A group of investors completed the acquisition of Electronic Arts, and reports say the deal left the company with about $20 billion in debt. This is a major industry development with potential long-term effects on EA’s structure and strategy.

items.title: Microsoft releases free Quake update tied to franchise anniversary
items.summary: Microsoft announced a free update for the Quake remaster as part of the series’ 30th anniversary, reinforcing the day’s broader wave of Quake-related news. The update includes fresh content for players of the modern remaster.

items.title: GTA 6 physical-media stance draws renewed attention
items.summary: Sony’s decision to stop manufacturing physical game discs in January 2028 prompted fresh discussion after commentary tied the move to Grand Theft Auto VI. The topic reflects a wider industry shift toward digital distribution.

items.title: Apex Legends security issue reportedly fixed
items.summary: Gaming coverage highlighted a security flaw in Apex Legends that reportedly allowed hackers to take control of player characters, followed by a fix. This is one of the more notable live-service game maintenance stories from the last day.

items.title: Rainbow Six Siege backend hack reported
items.summary: Reports say hackers seized control of Rainbow Six Siege’s backend and distributed billions of credits. The incident stands out as a major esports and competitive-game integrity concern.

items.title: Warhammer 40,000: Battlesector outlines upcoming DLC roadmap
items.summary: PC Gamer reported that Warhammer 40,000: Battlesector has a roadmap for new additions, including a narrative DLC. The announcement adds to the day’s stream of ongoing-support news for established games.

items.title: New Nintendo Switch 2 games and releases continue to surface
items.summary: Nintendo-related coverage also included news of Wild Blue Skies heading to the Switch eShop this autumn and other platform release updates. These announcements reflect continued momentum around Switch 2 software support.
